title: Chicken, prepackaged or deli, luncheon meat, reduced sodium

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken prepackaged or deli luncheon meat is a ready‑to‑eat product made from chicken breast that is processed for extended shelf life and convenience. The reduced‑sodium version (1008) contains about 30 % less salt than regular counterparts, making it a better choice for those monitoring sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken deli meats are commonly used as fillings for sandwiches, salads, and snack platters.
Sodium reduction is achieved through specialized salt substitutes and osmotic processing techniques.
The product is usually pasteurized, allowing storage at room temperature for several weeks.
Chicken is a lean source of high‑quality protein, popular among athletes.
In many countries these items are classified as “meat products” and are subject to specific food‑safety regulations.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Reduced sodium
items.content: Lower salt content helps maintain normal blood pressure for individuals limiting sodium.

items.title: Source of vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 supports amino‑acid metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports immune health.

items.title: Low‑calorie option
items.content: Compared with red meat, chicken deli meats are generally lower in calories, useful for weight management.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Preservative content
items.content: To extend shelf life, preservatives may be added, which can be problematic for sensitive people.

items.title: Possible nitrites
items.content: Certain formulations contain nitrites, which are best limited in large amounts.

items.title: Risk of contamination
items.content: As with any ready‑made meat product, improper storage can lead to bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the chicken deli meat thinly and use it in sandwiches, salads, wraps, or enjoy it as a snack. It can be gently warmed in a pan or microwave, but excessive heating may dry it out.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place at temperatures not exceeding 25 °C. Once opened, keep the product refrigerated and consume within 5–7 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
